exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Blocking
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers exploiting a bidirectional log ingestion path could block or manipulate indicators to suppress detection during ingestion.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: A bidirectional log ingestion path can be abused to enumerate log contents, exposing sensitive information or enabling further attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-Stage Channels
exploitedBy.relevance: A bidirectional ingestion path could serve as a covert multi-stage communication channel between attacker-controlled systems.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared credentials in the management plane are a prime target for abuse of cloud account access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Additional Cloud Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared credential trust in the management plane can be exploited to add or modify cloud credentials for persistent access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Secrets Management Stores
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared management plane credentials may grant access to cloud secrets stores, enabling credential harvesting across the environment.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly permissive egress rules allow attackers to exfiltrate data using alternative protocols that bypass intended controls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
exploitedBy.relevance: Permissive egress from a security zone enables exfiltration of data to external web services without restriction.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly permissive egress also allows attackers to transfer tools and payloads into the environment from external sources.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Event Triggered Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: SIEM action channels can be abused to trigger malicious execution by injecting crafted events that invoke automated responses.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Software Deployment Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: SIEM action channels with broad trust can be leveraged similarly to deployment tools to propagate malicious actions across systems.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Account Manipulation
exploitedBy.relevance: Trust propagation through SIEM channels could be exploited to manipulate accounts or escalate privileges across integrated systems.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient micro-segmentation allows attackers to bridge network boundaries and move laterally within the security layer.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Without proper micro-segmentation, attackers can exploit remote services to move laterally between components in the security layer.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of micro-segmentation enables network sniffing across security layer traffic, exposing sensitive communications.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Bypassing the API gateway often involves abuse of application access tokens to authenticate directly to SIEM APIs.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Application Integration
exploitedBy.relevance: Exploiting SIEM integration through API gateway bypass aligns with abusing cloud application integration points.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Deployment updates that misconfigure zone boundaries may inadvertently disable or alter cloud firewall rules protecting zone boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfiguration during deployment updates can result in system firewall rules being modified or disabled, exposing zone boundaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Devices
exploitedBy.relevance: Out-of-band management gaps often involve compromise of network devices that provide access to the management plane.
